sections.h2: Orangeburg County housing at a glance
sections.html:
Orangeburg County covers 1,127.89 square miles in the Midlands of South Carolina, and the city of Orangeburg is both the seat and the largest community. The 2020 census counted 84,223 residents. Farming, factories and two universities support the local economy, with manufacturing the biggest employer at 17.3% of jobs.

Someone selling in town and someone selling on a farm road down south are billed by the same county, yet they find different kinds of buyers. Farmland and inherited houses are common reasons to sell, and both come with tax deadlines worth knowing before you list.

sections.h2: Where to go and when taxes are due
sections.html:
Orangeburg County wants real property tax by January 15 and treats an account as delinquent from March 17. Motor vehicles run on their own calendar. Mailed payments are judged by postmark.

Office or detailContact
Assessor, street address1437 Amelia Street, Orangeburg, SC 29115
Assessor, mailing addressP.O. Box 9000, Attn: County Assessor, Orangeburg, SC 29116-9000
Assessor, phone803-533-6220
Delinquent Tax Collector counterMonday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

Before you drive over to pay, phone the Treasurer or the Delinquent Tax Collector to confirm how payment is taken.

Late charges come from S.C. Code 12-45-180: 3% for paying after January 15, 7% more before February 2 and 5% more before March 17, the date the account is delinquent.

The steps land only weeks apart, so a seller closing in January or February should request a payoff dated for the exact closing day.

Every five years the county reappraises, as S.C. Code 12-43-217 requires. Values can move up or down with the market, the property's condition and similar factors. An assessment notice is not a tax bill. Notices mostly arrive in the year after a value change, a corrected error, a transfer or a countywide reassessment. The Assessor can tell you the next cycle year.

Selling can trigger a separate reassessment, which the county labels an Assessable Transfer of Interest. It takes effect December 31 of the year the deed was conveyed. The 15% limit on yearly increases stopped applying to such transfers after the 2006 tax year, so expect the buyer's bill to reflect the sale and not your old value.

Appeals must be written and filed within 90 days of the assessment notice. With no notice that year, the cutoff moves to January 15, matching the first penalty date on the tax notice.

An appeal doesn't suspend payment. Penalties accrue if January 15 passes unpaid, and a refund follows only when an adjustment is granted.

  • Applications for agricultural classification, whether timberland or cropland, are due January 15, even from heirs who received the land during the tax year.
  • Switching farmland to another use can bring rollback taxes covering three years.
  • Send appeals to the Assessor, 803-533-6220.

Heirs holding farmland should get the agricultural application in ahead of January 15.

Owners who occupy their home may apply for the 4% legal residence rate, using a form on the Assessor's website. Under S.C. Code 12-43-220, other real property is assessed at 6%.

The lower rate extends to the house and up to five contiguous acres, but renting the house for over 72 days in a calendar year ends it. Say nothing for six months after losing eligibility and the owner risks a penalty equal to the tax paid, with interest at 0.5% monthly and a $30 minimum.

A buyer may assume the lower rate carries over. Confirm with the Assessor whether you had it, and encourage your buyer to apply.

The Delinquent Tax Collector may sell a property whose taxes stay unpaid. After the sale the owner has a year to buy it back. Real estate notices run for three weeks, while mobile homes are advertised for the final two.

The owner, a grantee from the owner, or a mortgage or judgment creditor can redeem. The total is all taxes, costs, assessments and penalties together with interest on the full bid, and that interest steps up by quarter:

  1. Months 1 to 3: 3%
  2. Months 4 to 6: 6%
  3. Months 7 to 9: 9%
  4. Months 10 to 12: 12%

Interest is capped at the bid submitted for the forfeited land commission. Mobile home owners who redeem also owe the bidder rent, limited to one-twelfth of the last completed year's taxes with a $10 monthly minimum. Throughout the year the bidder holds no ownership rights and may not enter. After it ends, the Tax Collector issues a tax deed as soon as possible.

Each $500 of value carries a $1.85 recording charge: $1.30 for the state, $0.55 for the county (S.C. Code 12-24-10 and 12-24-90). Section 12-24-40 exempts a deed in lieu of foreclosure and a foreclosure deed to the lender. Higher sale prices mean a higher fee, and your closing attorney or title company will quote the exact amount.

sections.h2: If you owe tax and want to sell
sections.html:
Unpaid tax is a closing-table item, not a deal killer. Whatever the county is owed comes out of your proceeds.

  • Mark the dates: January 15 for appeals and agricultural applications, March 17 for delinquency.
  • Request a payoff figure before March 17.
  • Learn whether the 4% rate was in place.

Cash Home Buyers purchases houses in their present state, so someone who can't afford repairs can still request an offer. Cash also skips the lender appraisal and the mortgage approval wait, a plus for an estate or an older house that needs work. Collect the county figures first and you'll see what the proceeds look like.

Rural parcels need extra care. If the land carries an agricultural classification, a change of use can bring three years of rollback taxes, and the January 15 application date applies to heirs as well. Before signing a contract, ask the Assessor how the sale and the buyer's plans affect the classification.

For a family-owned house, start with the Assessor at 803-533-6220 to confirm who is the owner of record, where bills go and which rate applies. The mailing address for correspondence is P.O. Box 9000 in Orangeburg.

Estates often sit for a year or more, and taxes keep coming due on January 15 whether or not the title is settled. Compare the unpaid balance with the likely price early, so the family knows what will be left after the county is paid.

sections.h2: What to bring and how to prepare
sections.html:
Take the property address or parcel details, photo ID and, for an estate, proof that you may act for the owner. Visit the Assessor at 1437 Amelia Street or call 803-533-6220. The Delinquent Tax Collector's counter keeps weekday hours from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

Ask each office for figures in writing when possible, note the name of the person who gave them and share them with your title company. If a closing slips into a new penalty period, ask for an updated payoff before the day you sign.

sections.h2: Timing a sale around the January and March dates
sections.html:
Two dates drive most decisions here. January 15 is the due date and the cutoff for appeals when no notice was mailed. March 17 is when unpaid real property taxes turn delinquent. A sale that closes ahead of the first date is simplest, since the payoff is just the base bill.

If you list in late winter, expect penalties to be part of the payoff. That is manageable when the price is well above the debt. When it is not, call the Delinquent Tax Collector early and ask what the county needs to release the parcel at closing.

faqs.q: What is the due date for real property tax in Orangeburg County?
faqs.a: January 15. After March 17 the account is delinquent.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal an Orangeburg County assessment?
faqs.a: Ninety days from the assessment notice. If none was issued, file by January 15, the first penalty date.

faqs.q: Will an appeal in Orangeburg County hold off my tax payment?
faqs.a: No. Pay by January 15 or penalties still apply.

faqs.q: How much time do I have to redeem after an Orangeburg County tax sale?
faqs.a: A full year from the sale date, with interest of 3%, 6%, 9% or 12% depending on the quarter.

faqs.q: Can an Orangeburg County house with back taxes be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. Closing pays the taxes out of the proceeds, and Cash Home Buyers can buy the house in its current condition.
